anomalies.observed: R60 connects Net-(D30-K2) to ESTOP_OUT, and D30.4 (A2) is also on ESTOP_OUT. Both terminals of the D30 second LED section therefore sit on the same net, so no current can flow through that LED. Its partner R59 returns its cathode to GND.
anomalies.expected: An ESTOP_OUT indicator LED should have its anode on ESTOP_OUT and its cathode returned through a current-limit resistor to GND, as the K1 leg does with R59.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The ESTOP_OUT indicator LED channel is dead, so the e-stop output gives no visual indication on that path. The loop does not create a short to a supply.

anomalies.observed: The LTC4412 ideal-diode P-FET Q1 has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. U6 VIN, the input supply, is on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE is on +5V. The P-FET's body diode therefore conducts from +5V back to VBUS.
anomalies.expected: For reverse-current blocking, the P-FET source should be on the input supply (VIN / USBC_VBUS_IN) and the drain on the load (+5V, the SENSE node). The body diode should then block +5V-to-VBUS current. The spec says this circuit exists to provide reverse-current protection.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) ... Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: Reverse current from the +5V rail can flow back to the USB-C VBUS input through the FET body diode. This defeats the reverse-current protection that the ideal-diode stage is meant to provide.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows two plausible defects: the ESTOP_OUT indicator LED D30 is shorted by R60 returning to ESTOP_OUT, and the LTC4412 P-FET Q1 has its source and drain reversed relative to the VIN/SENSE topology, which breaks reverse-current blocking. Both are inferred from connectivity and standard practice, and neither is confirmed against the reference design.
